reference.label: Fibre cut
reference.definition: A physical discontinuity in a fibre span that prevents optical propagation.
reference.example: An excavator cuts an incoming span, leaving the next amplifier with no input light.

reference.label: Span loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in fibre-span attenuation caused by bending, splice damage, stress, or similar degradation.
reference.example: A damaged splice adds 12 dB of loss and leaves downstream channels at low power.

reference.label: Disconnected optical jumper
reference.definition: A connector or patch cord disconnected from an optical port or patch panel.
reference.example: A technician unplugs the OMS input jumper and the pre-amplifier loses its optical feed.

reference.label: Contaminated connector
reference.definition: Contamination on an optical connector that introduces loss or reflection.
reference.example: Cleaning a dirty patch-panel connector removes the channel's elevated pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: Amplifier failure
reference.definition: A hard amplifier or pump failure that produces no usable optical output.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier loses its pump and all wavelengths disappear from its output.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: An amplifier gain deficiency relative to its configured set point.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier supplies 3 dB less gain than provisioned.

reference.label: Amplifier noise-figure degradation
reference.definition: An increase in amplifier noise figure that lowers OSNR even when output power remains normal.
reference.example: An ageing EDFA maintains target power but adds a 2 dB OSNR penalty.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A wavelength-dependent gain imbalance across an amplifier's optical band.
reference.example: Long-wavelength channels leave an EDFA 4 dB weaker than centre-band channels.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive pump-laser wear evidenced by rising drive current needed to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 123% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Transmit laser failure
reference.definition: A hard transmitter-laser fault that removes the emitted optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder laser fails, producing no channel light at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Card failure
reference.definition: A hard equipment failure that prevents a circuit card from performing its traffic or monitoring functions.
reference.example: A line-card ASIC fails, dropping traffic and stopping valid telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local optical or electronic penalty that raises errors without propagating along the path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver develops excess pre-FEC errors while neighbouring channels remain healthy.

reference.label: Transmit laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmitter-laser deterioration evidenced by rising bias current before hard failure.
reference.example: Laser bias rises from 100% to 121% of its beginning-of-life value over several months.

reference.label: Channel margin erosion
reference.definition: A slow reduction in an optical channel's remaining performance margin.
reference.example: A channel's measured margin falls from 4 dB to 1.5 dB over several months.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A gradual change in one WSS channel's actual attenuation relative to its configured value.
reference.example: A channel configured for 3 dB attenuation slowly drifts to 6 dB.

reference.label: WSS passband offset
reference.definition: A frequency displacement of a WSS channel passband from the intended carrier centre.
reference.example: A WSS passband shifts 5 GHz and clips one side of the coherent signal.

reference.label: WSS passband narrowing
reference.definition: A reduction in usable WSS bandwidth that clips a channel spectrum.
reference.example: A nominal 50 GHz passband contracts to 38 GHz and degrades the signal.

reference.label: WSS ingress-port failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of one WSS ingress port that blocks all channels entering through that port.
reference.example: The west ingress module fails while traffic on other ROADM degrees remains operational.

reference.label: ROADM ingress-port blockage
reference.definition: A ROADM ingress state or configuration that prevents light from entering an onward path without requiring port hardware failure.
reference.example: An inadvertently closed ingress blocks one wavelength from reaching the downstream receiver.

reference.label: DGD increase
reference.definition: An increase in differential group delay that can exceed coherent-receiver tolerance.
reference.example: A polarization event raises DGD from 8 ps to 35 ps.

reference.label: Fast SOP transient
reference.definition: A state-of-polarization change faster than a coherent receiver can track.
reference.example: Rapid fibre polarization rotation causes a burst of errored seconds.
synonyms: fast SOP change beyond tracking speed

reference.label: Mechanical fibre disturbance
reference.definition: A brief physical disturbance of fibre or patching that causes a short optical-loss excursion.
reference.example: Movement of a patch panel produces a sub-second power dip.

reference.label: Channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief OMS power excursion caused by channels being added or removed.
reference.example: Adding several wavelengths produces a short aggregate-power swing.

reference.label: Protection-switch hit
reference.definition: A brief client interruption while protection selection changes from one path to another.
reference.example: An SNCP switch causes a 30 ms interruption before traffic resumes on protection.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that interrupts traversing ODUs.
reference.example: A fabric plane fails and affected cross-connections emit ODU-AIS.

reference.label: ODU misconnection
reference.definition: An incorrect OTN cross-connect that delivers an ODU to an unintended destination.
reference.example: An ODU intended for port A is delivered to port B and triggers a trace mismatch.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: A hard failure of a client-facing port or its optic that interrupts the associated service.
reference.example: A failed 100GbE client optic takes its service down.

reference.label: Instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring instrument reports a value that does not represent the actual condition.
reference.example: A power monitor reports −20 dBm while an independent meter reads −10 dBm.

reference.label: Stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitor repeatedly reports an old frozen value instead of current measurements.
reference.example: Received-power telemetry remains unchanged after the fibre is disconnected.

reference.label: Unspecified upstream-path failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure anywhere before the observing receiver on the optical signal path.
reference.example: A receiver loses light, but documentation identifies only an unspecified upstream failure.

reference.label: Unspecified server-path failure
reference.definition: An unspecified failure in a layer or resource on which an ODU service path depends.
reference.example: A defect on the active ODU path causes the client selector to choose protection.
synonyms: any failure on the active ODU path

reference.label: Optical signal loss
reference.definition: No detectable optical signal, or power below the receiver's detection threshold.
reference.example: A disconnected transmitter fibre leaves the far-end receiver with no detectable input light.

reference.label: Low optical power
reference.definition: Optical power below its expected level at a channel, receiver, or aggregate interface.
reference.example: Edge-band channels arrive 3 dB below their expected receiver power.

reference.label: No output light
reference.definition: An optical device emits no usable output despite being expected to transmit or amplify.
reference.example: An EDFA has normal input power but zero measured output power.

reference.label: OSC loss
reference.definition: Failure to receive the optical supervisory channel on an incoming span.
reference.example: A span cut makes the downstream amplifier report that its OSC is not received.

reference.label: Optical power excursion
reference.definition: A brief optical-power dip or swing lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Mechanical movement causes a half-second 4 dB power dip.

reference.label: Low OSNR
reference.definition: An optical signal-to-noise ratio below its expected or acceptable level.
reference.example: Signal power is restored by levelling, but a 2 dB OSNR penalty remains.

reference.label: High DGD
reference.definition: Differential group delay elevated enough to reduce coherent-channel performance.
reference.example: The receiver observes 35 ps DGD and begins recording errors.

reference.label: Optical filter penalty
reference.definition: Signal-quality loss from spectral narrowing or misalignment while optical power may remain normal.
reference.example: A shifted WSS filter raises pre-FEC BER even though channel power is unchanged.

reference.label: Receiver penalty
reference.definition: A signal-quality penalty introduced locally by the receiver and not propagated downstream.
reference.example: Only one receiver reports reduced margin on an otherwise healthy lightpath.

reference.label: Unit down
reference.definition: A failed equipment unit that carries no traffic and reports no valid monitoring values.
reference.example: A dead line card drops its traffic and stops updating telemetry.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: Loss of OTU frame alignment at a line receiver, with or without optical light present.
reference.example: Severely degraded OSNR destroys OTU frame lock while input light remains present.

reference.label: OTU signal degradation
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors above the signal-degrade threshold while OTU framing remains aligned.
reference.example: A receiver raises signal degrade while remaining frame-locked.

reference.label: Errored second
reference.definition: A one-second interval containing one or more qualifying transmission errors.
reference.example: A polarization transient produces five errored seconds.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An alarm-indication signal carried downstream on an affected ODU path.
reference.example: After OTU frame loss, the receiver inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU.

reference.label: OTU backward defect indication
reference.definition: A backward indication sent toward the transmitter when the far-end receiver detects an OTU defect.
reference.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns OTU-BDI to the transmitting endpoint.

reference.label: Misdirected ODU
reference.definition: An ODU received at the wrong destination because of incorrect cross-connect routing.
reference.example: ODU2 from port 1 emerges at port 7 instead of port 5.

reference.label: Client service down
reference.definition: A client service unavailable in at least one traffic direction.
reference.example: A failed client port interrupts the attached 100GbE service.

reference.label: Received traffic loss
reference.definition: Traffic arriving at a receiver or card is no longer recoverable or available.
reference.example: A receive-side card failure stops local traffic recovery.

reference.label: Monitoring silent
reference.definition: An affected resource supplies no current monitoring status or measurements.
reference.example: A failed card stops updating power and performance counters.

reference.label: Traffic alarms masked
reference.definition: Traffic-layer alarms are suppressed because an equipment alarm already identifies the root fault.
reference.example: A card-failure alarm suppresses consequent OTU loss-of-frame indications.
synonyms: traffic alarms masked by equipment alarm

reference.label: All channels lost
reference.definition: Every wavelength in an affected optical aggregate is absent.
reference.example: A dead line amplifier removes all 80 channels from the outgoing span.

reference.label: Unaffected operation
reference.definition: Resources outside the specifically impaired scope continue to operate normally.
reference.example: One WSS ingress fails while channels on the other degrees remain operational.

reference.label: Normal output power
reference.definition: Output power remains within its expected range despite another quality impairment.
reference.example: A noisy EDFA maintains target output power while channel OSNR declines.

reference.label: Signal-quality degradation
reference.definition: Reduced recoverable channel quality without necessarily implying complete signal loss.
reference.example: A channel retains normal power but has reduced margin and elevated pre-FEC BER.

reference.label: Gain outside target tolerance
reference.definition: Measured amplifier gain differs from its provisioned target by more than the allowed tolerance.
reference.example: Measured gain is 16.5 dB against a 19 dB target.
synonyms: gain more than 2 dB from target

reference.label: High laser-bias threshold
reference.definition: Transmit-laser bias current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life reference.
reference.example: A bias reading of 122% satisfies the high-bias condition.
synonyms: LBC above 120% of beginning of life

reference.label: High pump-current threshold
reference.definition: Amplifier pump current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life reference.
reference.example: A pump-current reading of 124% satisfies the end-of-life threshold.
synonyms: PUMP-I above 120% of beginning of life

reference.label: Transmit-laser fault detected
reference.definition: An equipment diagnostic has detected an internal or output failure of the transmit laser.
reference.example: The card detects absent laser output despite an enable command.

reference.label: Blocked ingress
reference.definition: An ingress path prevents all channels entering through it from passing onward.
reference.example: A failed west-degree WSS ingress blocks every arriving wavelength.

reference.label: No optical-layer symptom
reference.definition: An ODU-layer defect exists while optical power and optical-quality indicators remain normal.
reference.example: A misconnected ODU raises a trace mismatch with normal wavelength power.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver, optionally summarized in performance bins.
reference.example: A line receiver reports −14.2 dBm received power.

reference.label: Composite amplifier input power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all wavelengths entering an amplifier.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier reports −8 dBm composite input power.

reference.label: Composite amplifier output power
reference.definition: Total optical power of all wavelengths leaving an amplifier.
reference.example: An amplifier reports +18 dBm composite output power.

reference.label: Pump drive current
reference.definition: Amplifier pump-laser drive current, commonly expressed as a percentage of beginning-of-life current.
reference.example: The amplifier reports pump current at 123% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Transmit laser-bias current
reference.definition: Transmitter-laser bias current, commonly expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transponder reports laser bias at 121%.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for an individual wavelength.
reference.example: A ROADM channel monitor reports channel 22 at −6 dBm.

reference.label: Channel OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio for a channel, measured by an OCM or estimated by a coherent receiver.
reference.example: The channel is reported with an OSNR of 18.5 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC BER
reference.definition: Bit-error ratio measured before forward-error correction at a coherent receiver.
reference.example: The receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-3.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: Delay difference between the polarization modes of a coherent optical signal.
reference.example: The coherent DSP estimates DGD at 35 ps.

reference.label: SOP rate of change
reference.definition: The measured rate at which the received state of polarization changes.
reference.example: A spike in SOP rate coincides with several errored seconds.

reference.label: Line errored-seconds counter
reference.definition: A performance counter for errored seconds on a transport line, commonly reported in 15-minute bins.
reference.example: The line records 12 errored seconds in the current 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Client errored-seconds counter
reference.definition: A performance counter for errored seconds observed on a client signal.
reference.example: The client interface records five errored seconds in a 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Client unavailable-seconds counter
reference.definition: A performance counter measuring time for which a client service is unavailable.
reference.example: A one-minute outage accumulates 60 client unavailable seconds.

reference.label: OSC receiver status
reference.definition: Status indicating whether an incoming optical supervisory channel is being received and decoded.
reference.example: After a span cut, OSC receiver status changes from received to not received.

reference.label: Alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor that raises status or alarms without exposing a numerical measurement value.
reference.example: An OSC receiver reports loss status but no measured signal value.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: An erbium-doped fibre amplifier used to restore or launch optical power on a line.
reference.example: An EDFA provides 18 dB gain while monitoring composite input and output power.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the transmitting end of an OMS.
reference.example: A booster launches the multiplexed signal into a long outgoing span.

reference.label: In-line amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at an intermediate site between OMS endpoints.
reference.example: An in-line amplifier restores level at a mid-span hut.

reference.label: Pre-amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of an OMS.
reference.example: A pre-amplifier boosts weak incoming channels before demultiplexing.

reference.label: Coherent line interface
reference.definition: A coherent optical interface that terminates an optical channel.
reference.example: A coherent line interface reports receive power, BER, OSNR, DGD, and SOP rate.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: A line-interface type that maps a client signal onto a coherent optical channel.
reference.example: A 400G transponder terminates one coherent wavelength.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: A line-interface type that aggregates multiple client signals onto one optical channel.
reference.example: A 400G muxponder combines several clients onto a coherent carrier.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A line-interface card that terminates an OTU and its contained ODUs.
reference.example: An OTN line card raises signal degrade when pre-FEC errors exceed threshold.

reference.label: VA-TPD-400
reference.definition: The VA model of 400G coherent transponder.
reference.example: A VA-TPD-400 terminates and monitors a 400G wavelength.

reference.label: VA-MXP-200
reference.definition: The VA model of 200G coherent muxponder.
reference.example: A VA-MXP-200 aggregates clients onto a 200G line signal.

reference.label: VA-MXP-400
reference.definition: The VA model of 400G coherent muxponder.
reference.example: A VA-MXP-400 reports OSNR and laser-bias telemetry for its carrier.

reference.label: VA-OTN-LC-200
reference.definition: The VA model of 200G OTN line card.
reference.example: A VA-OTN-LC-200 terminates a 200G OTU.

reference.label: VA-OTN-LC-400
reference.definition: The VA model of 400G OTN line card.
reference.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 detects high DGD on a 400G OTU.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: A reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer that routes wavelengths between line degrees.
reference.example: A CDC ROADM independently routes wavelengths to east and north degrees.

reference.label: WSS degree module
reference.definition: A wavelength-selective-switch module serving one ROADM line degree.
reference.example: A four-degree ROADM uses a separate WSS module for each degree.

reference.label: OTN cross-connect switch
reference.definition: An OTN resource whose switching fabric cross-connects ODUs between interfaces.
reference.example: An OTN switch routes an ODU2 between two line cards.

reference.label: Client interface port
reference.definition: A client-facing interface that maps a customer signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GbE client port maps customer traffic into an ODU.

reference.label: OCH_LOS
reference.definition: An optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm indicating no detectable light at one receiver.
reference.example: A disconnected channel fibre causes the receiver to raise OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU_LOF
reference.definition: An OTU loss-of-frame alarm indicating that a receiver cannot recover OTU framing.
reference.example: Severe OSNR degradation causes OTU_LOF while optical light remains present.

reference.label: OTU_SD
reference.definition: An OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when errors exceed threshold while framing remains aligned.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU_BDI
reference.definition: The reported indication that a far-end receiver has returned an OTU backward defect indication.
reference.example: The local transmitter reports OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses frame.

reference.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating a detected internal transmit-laser failure.
reference.example: A transmitter with no laser output raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating a card-level hardware failure.
reference.example: A line-card ASIC failure raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
reference.definition: An ageing alarm indicating transmit-laser bias above its configured high threshold.
reference.example: Laser bias at 122% of beginning-of-life triggers LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

reference.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
reference.definition: An amplifier input loss-of-signal alarm indicating absent incoming optical light.
reference.example: A pulled OMS jumper causes the pre-amplifier to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OSC_LOS
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the incoming span's optical supervisory channel is not received.
reference.example: A cut between amplifier huts causes the downstream hut to raise OSC_LOS.

reference.label: AMP_FAIL
reference.definition: An amplifier alarm indicating that the device has no optical output.
reference.example: A complete pump failure drives output to zero and raises AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
reference.definition: An amplifier alarm indicating measured gain outside the permitted target tolerance.
reference.example: Gain of 16 dB against a 19 dB target raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
reference.definition: An amplifier ageing alarm indicating pump current beyond its end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump current at 125% of beginning-of-life raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: CLIENT_SF
reference.definition: A client signal-fail alarm indicating failure of the associated client service.
reference.example: Failure of the active ODU path causes the client port to raise CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU_AIS indication
reference.definition: A reported indication that ODU alarm indication signal is being received.
reference.example: A client port reports ODU_AIS after an upstream OTU frame loss.

reference.label: ODU_BDI
reference.definition: A reported ODU backward-defect indication for an associated ODU connection.
reference.example: A remote ODU defect causes the local client port to report ODU_BDI.

reference.label: ODU_TIM
reference.definition: An ODU trail-trace mismatch alarm commonly indicating a misconnection.
reference.example: An ODU delivered to the wrong client port triggers ODU_TIM.

reference.label: PROT_ACTIVE
reference.definition: A protection alarm indicating that the protection path is currently carrying the service.
reference.example: After working-path failure, the selector switches and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
reference.definition: A protection alarm indicating that a protection path is unavailable.
reference.example: Failure of the standby ODU path raises PROT_UNAVAIL while working traffic continues.

reference.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating hard failure of a local client interface port.
reference.example: A failed 400GbE client interface raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
reference.definition: An alarm indicating failure of an OTN switch's internal cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A switch loses a fabric plane and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

reference.label: One optical channel
reference.definition: A single optical wavelength rather than the complete multiplex.
reference.example: A filter shift degrades channel 37 while adjacent channels remain normal.

reference.label: All optical channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength in the affected OMS, OTS, or ingress aggregate.
reference.example: A dead amplifier removes every channel from its outgoing fibre.

reference.label: Some optical channels
reference.definition: A proper subset of wavelengths in a multiplexed signal.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens only channels near the long-wavelength band edge.

reference.label: One ingress port
reference.definition: All channels arriving through one ROADM degree's input port.
reference.example: A west ingress failure blocks its channels but not those on other degrees.

reference.label: Local unit
reference.definition: The equipment unit itself rather than its carried traffic.
reference.example: Pump-current ageing is confined to the local amplifier card.

reference.label: One receiver
reference.definition: The particular receiving endpoint observing a local defect.
reference.example: Receiver degradation affects one coherent receiver only.

reference.label: All traversing ODUs
reference.definition: Every ODU carried by the affected OTU or cross-connected through the affected switch.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupts every ODU traversing the switch.

reference.label: One ODU
reference.definition: A single ODU trail or connection.
reference.example: A bad cross-connect misroutes one ODU while other ODUs remain correct.

reference.label: One client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing service associated with a particular client connection.
reference.example: A port failure affects the attached 100GbE service.

reference.label: Other ROADM degrees
reference.definition: ROADM line directions other than the specifically affected degree.
reference.example: A west-degree fault leaves north, south, and east degrees unaffected.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting toward the observing receiver.
reference.example: No light at the local receiver is traced to the far-end transmitter.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the signal emitted by the local transmitter.
reference.example: A local laser failure appears as signal loss at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Local resource
reference.definition: The current equipment resource that reports or contains a condition.
reference.example: The pump-ageing indication is localized to the reporting amplifier.

reference.label: Local port
reference.definition: The particular local interface port reporting or containing a condition.
reference.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL localizes the fault to the reporting client port.

reference.label: Receiver
reference.definition: The receiving function where optical quality, margin, and errors are observed.
reference.example: A slow margin decline becomes visible at the coherent receiver.

reference.label: Upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any point before the observing unit along the incoming signal path, including its source.
reference.example: A contaminated connector two nodes before the receiver lies on the upstream path.

reference.label: Incoming span
reference.definition: The fibre span immediately preceding and terminating at the observing site.
reference.example: OSC loss at Hut B is associated with the incoming span from Hut A.

reference.label: Upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The immediately preceding amplifier on the signal path.
reference.example: No input light at the current site is traced to the upstream amplifier.

reference.label: OMS input
reference.definition: The patch or physical connection where an optical multiplex section enters a unit.
reference.example: A jumper is disconnected at the pre-amplifier's OMS input.

reference.label: Upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The relevant channel or ingress port at the immediately preceding ROADM.
reference.example: Low power is first observed on the channel at the upstream ROADM.

reference.label: Downstream
reference.definition: Later in the direction of signal or traffic propagation.
reference.example: An amplifier's OSNR penalty remains visible at downstream receivers.
synonyms: on the path to the far end

reference.label: Optical band edge
reference.definition: One frequency extreme of the supported optical band.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens channels near the long-wavelength band edge.

reference.label: Switch on the ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN cross-connect traversed by an ODU service path.
reference.example: A misconnection at an intermediate switch sends the ODU to the wrong destination.

reference.label: Active ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU path currently selected to carry a protected service.
reference.example: A defect on the active path causes the selector to move traffic.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The ODU route designated as the normal working member of a protected pair.
reference.example: A working-path defect causes SNCP to select protection.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The standby ODU route intended to protect the working path.
reference.example: A defect on the protection path reduces redundancy while working traffic continues.

reference.label: Either service endpoint
reference.definition: Either of the two terminating client ports of an end-to-end service.
reference.example: Failure of a client optic at either endpoint can take the service down.

reference.label: Standard monitoring
reference.definition: Base monitoring available without specialized options, including alarms and ordinary performance counters.
reference.example: Errored seconds are supplied in standard 15-minute bins.

reference.label: Power monitoring option
reference.definition: An entitlement or fitted option exposing optical input, output, or received-power measurements.
reference.example: Enabling power monitoring exposes amplifier composite input and output power.

reference.label: Advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: An entitlement exposing coherent-DSP metrics and equipment-health currents.
reference.example: Advanced monitoring exposes DGD, SOP rate, and laser-bias telemetry.

reference.label: Optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: An entitlement or facility exposing per-channel power and OSNR at a ROADM.
reference.example: An enabled OCM reports power and OSNR for every wavelength.

reference.label: Hard fault
reference.definition: An abrupt failure that normally causes immediate traffic or signal loss.
reference.example: A fibre cut is a hard fault because light disappears immediately.

reference.label: Soft impairment
reference.definition: A partial degradation in which traffic may continue with reduced quality.
reference.example: A noise-figure rise is soft because power remains present while OSNR worsens.

reference.label: Incipient deterioration
reference.definition: A slow trend that precedes likely failure while traffic is not yet materially affected.
reference.example: Rising laser-bias current is an incipient deterioration.

reference.label: Transient event
reference.definition: A brief event lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: A short channel-loading power swing is transient.

reference.label: Critical
reference.definition: The highest operational alarm class used for defects directly threatening signal, equipment, or service.
reference.example: Optical-channel loss of signal is classified as critical.

reference.label: Major
reference.definition: A serious alarm class below critical requiring prompt operational attention.
reference.example: Loss of span supervision is classified as major.

reference.label: Minor
reference.definition: An alarm class for degradation, ageing, or reduced protection that may not interrupt service.
reference.example: A high laser-bias ageing alarm is classified as minor.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported condition or consequential indication that does not itself create an active alarm.
reference.example: A backward defect indication is reported without separate alarm severity.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, ODU-AIS is sent on contained ODUs and OTU-BDI is returned toward the transmitter.
reference.example: Loss of an OTU carrying four ODUs inserts AIS into all four and returns OTU-BDI.

reference.label: Per-span OSC regeneration
reference.definition: Each amplifier site terminates the incoming OSC and originates a separate OSC on the next span.
reference.example: Loss of the A-to-B OSC does not prevent site B from launching its OSC toward C.
synonyms: OSC failure confined to its span

reference.label: SNCP path protection
reference.definition: A receiver selects between working and protection ODU paths and can use a defect-free alternative.
reference.example: When the working ODU develops AIS, the selector chooses the healthy protection ODU.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM routing
reference.definition: A ROADM switches wavelengths independently, so an ingress-wide impairment follows each routed channel.
reference.example: Weak west-ingress channels continue separately onto north and east egress degrees.

reference.label: Impairment pass-through
reference.definition: An arriving condition traverses a network element without being removed or materially changed.
reference.example: Low OSNR passes through an amplifier even when signal power is restored.

reference.label: Default condition handling
reference.definition: An input condition not covered by a more specific rule is handled by the element's default propagation behavior.
reference.example: Unclassified input spectral ripple is passed to the output unchanged.

reference.label: Optical power levelling
reference.definition: A node restores optical level toward its target without necessarily repairing quality penalties.
reference.example: A ROADM restores channel power while the earlier OSNR penalty remains.

reference.label: Automatic gain control
reference.definition: An amplifier operating mode that adjusts pump drive to maintain a configured gain.
reference.example: An EDFA increases pump current after input power falls to preserve its gain.

reference.label: Span-matched gain provisioning
reference.definition: An amplifier commissioning rule that sets target gain to compensate the associated fibre-span loss.
reference.example: An amplifier feeding an 18 dB span is provisioned for 18 dB gain.

reference.label: AGC response to input-power drop
reference.definition: The amplifier response to reduced input power, potentially restoring level while retaining an OSNR penalty.
reference.example: AGC restores output after a 5 dB input drop, but downstream OSNR remains degraded.
synonyms: under AGC, a drop of input level
